sources.title: Microsoft — Xbox Accessibility Guideline 118 (photosensitivity)
load_bearing: 'A flash is defined as a 10% change in luminance (where 100% is the maximum luminance of a white screen)'; 'The darker luminance value should be below 0.8.'
Failure: 'Flashes occur too frequently (approximately more than three per second)'; 'Flashes take up a certain amount of the screen (approximately 20 percent or more)'
Red flash: applies when either extreme is saturated red (R/(R+G+B) >= 0.8); flash when change in (R-G-B) x 320 is greater than 20
Spatial pattern failure: alternating high-contrast bands, contrast difference > 10 percent, over ~20 percent or more of screen
'eliminating game content that can potentially cause photosensitive seizures is preferred over splash-screen warnings'
Tool listed: Harding FPA Test (Cambridge Research Systems)
'All games should be tested for photosensitive seizure triggers, regardless of whether the game includes intentional flashing.'

sources.title: GDC 2022 — An Overview of the 'Diablo II: Resurrected' Renderer (Kevin Todisco, Blizzard)
sources.read: full-fetch of the vault entry (talk description; video not viewed)

Covers why a custom 3D renderer was built from scratch: lighting, skin rendering, HDR color grading, order-independent transparency

sources.title: Diablo II: Resurrected developer interviews on the remaster architecture
load_bearing: A new physically based renderer was written on top of the old game logic; models replace sprites on the render layer
'Under the hood, all of the logic and simulation is still being run by sprites' — still a grid-based game
Animation framerate unlocked per-animation on the render layer to match original timing and feel, using the original sprite data

sources.title: Diablo II animation formats — COF / DCC / DC6 (Phrozen Keep, OpenDiablo2, Paul Siramy)
sources.read: full-fetch of annex + search-result summaries of the wider corpus
load_bearing: Mode tokens confirmed: NU (neutral), WL (walk), RN (run), A1/A2 (attack), BL (block), SC (cast), TH (throw), KK (kick), S1-S4 (skills), GH (get hit), DT (death), DD (corpse), TN (town neutral), TW (town walk); KB (knockback) reuses GH
COF 'mostly handles the drawing order of DCC for a given unit / mode / weapon class / direction / frame'
'Commonly, animations can be found with 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32 directions'; maximum 32; DC6 static / DCC animated
Example: an 8-direction 96-frame animation = 12 frames per direction

sources.title: Diablo II DT1 / DS1 tile formats and per-act palettes (Phrozen Keep knowledge base)
load_bearing: Tile classes: Floors, Animated Floors, Walls, Walls-into-abyss (drawn below floors), Roofs, Shadows, Special (warp) tiles
Orientation codes: 0 floors, 1-2 walls, 10-11 special, 13 shadows, 15 roofs
Each act uses a different palette; moving tiles between acts requires re-palettising
Multiple tiles may share a combination; the game picks one at random -> variation is authored, not procedural

sources.title: Autotiling — blob-47 bitmask and marching-squares tile sets
sources.read: search-result summary; corroborated by Excalibur.js and Godot/Tiled/RPG Maker convention
load_bearing: 8-neighbour bitmask; a diagonal counts only if both adjacent cardinals are present -> exactly 47 unique configurations
Marching squares uses a 4-bit N/E/S/W mask -> 16 tiles
Supported natively by Godot, Tiled, RPG Maker; isometric variants exist

sources.title: Godot 4 — NinePatchRect class reference
load_bearing: 'A control that displays a texture by keeping its corners intact, but tiling its edges and center.'
patch_margin_left/right/top/bottom define the 3x3 grid
Axis stretch modes STRETCH / TILE / TILE_FIT; TILE requires seamless textures
Authoring consequence: corners fixed, edge+centre must survive tiling or stretching

sources.title: Godot 4 — Importing images (compression, mipmaps, resolution)
load_bearing: VRAM compression: 'This mode should be avoided for 2D as it exhibits noticeable artifacts, especially for lower-resolution textures.'
'Lossless: This is the default and most common compression mode for 2D assets'
Mipmaps in 2D: 'this should only be enabled if your project visibly benefits from having mipmaps enabled' (~33% memory increase)
Recommends authoring from a high base resolution rather than downscaling textures during gameplay
TextureAtlas 'reduce[s] memory usage for animated 2D sprites'

sources.title: VFX overdraw / fill-rate budgets for translucent sprites and particles
sources.read: search-result summary; corroborated across multiple VFX production guides
load_bearing: Desktop budget ~500-800 active particles in view; mobile 150-300
Overdraw is the dominant cost for overlapping translucent sprites; pixels can be written 10-50x
Additive blending cheaper than alpha blending on mobile; additive avoids depth sorting
Transparent pixels in a texture still cost fill rate -> trim empty margins in the atlas

sources.title: Temporal consistency failure taxonomy in generated animation

sources.title: Perceptual hashing and embedding-distance approaches to generated-image similarity / infringement detection
sources.read: search-result summaries only (abstracts, not full text)
load_bearing: Perceptual hashes survive resize/compression/crop/colour adjustment; deployed at platform scale for near-duplicate detection
CLIP embeddings + MSE between anchor and generated embeddings used as a semantic-similarity metric
One reported combined RoI + image-hashing model: 88.7% infringement identification, false positives reduced 91.8% -> 2.8%
Note: every model-backed metric is a dependency decision on this host (no torch / onnxruntime) per sibling R8 finding
